books.title: Much Ado About Nothing
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.desc: In sunny Messina, two sworn enemies of love, Beatrice and Benedick, trade insults, while a malicious plot threatens the young lovers Claudio and Hero.
about: Don Pedro, Prince of Aragon, and his soldiers return from war to the house of Leonato, governor of Messina. The young lord Claudio falls in love with Leonato's gentle daughter Hero, and a wedding is quickly arranged. Meanwhile Hero's cousin Beatrice and the soldier Benedick, who both mock love and marriage, carry on their "merry war" of wit, and their friends decide to trick them into falling in love. But Don Pedro's resentful brother, Don John, is plotting to wreck Claudio's happiness.

Shakespeare's comedy mixes sparkling verbal sparring with deception, slander and reconciliation. Beatrice and Benedick are among his most beloved characters, and the bumbling constable Dogberry adds broad comedy.

Much Ado About Nothing is thought to have been written in 1598–1599 and was first printed in quarto in 1600. This edition offers the English text (from the First Folio, in its original spelling) and the French translation by François Guizot.

books.title: The Merchant of Venice
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.desc: To help his friend win the heiress Portia, a Venetian merchant borrows money from the moneylender Shylock, pledging a pound of his own flesh.
about: Bassanio, a young Venetian with no money, wants to court Portia, a rich and clever heiress of Belmont. His devoted friend Antonio, a merchant whose fortune is tied up in ships at sea, borrows three thousand ducats for him from the Jewish moneylender Shylock, whom he has often insulted. Shylock agrees to the loan on one condition: if it is not repaid on time, he may take a pound of Antonio's flesh.

The play mixes romantic comedy, with Portia's caskets and her disguise as a lawyer, and a dark drama of revenge, mercy and justice. Its portrayal of Shylock and the treatment he receives reflect the antisemitism of Shakespeare's time; Shylock's famous speech asking "Hath not a Jew eyes?" has long fuelled debate about how the play should be read and performed.

The Merchant of Venice is believed to have been written between 1596 and 1598 and was first printed in 1600. This edition offers the English text (from the First Folio, in its original spelling), the French translation by François Guizot and the German translation by August Wilhelm von Schlegel.

books.title: Julius Caesar
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.desc: Fearing that Caesar will become a tyrant, Brutus joins a conspiracy to assassinate him, and Rome is plunged into civil war.
about: Julius Caesar returns to Rome in triumph, and some senators fear he means to make himself king. The envious Cassius persuades the noble and idealistic Brutus, Caesar's friend, to join a conspiracy against him. Ignoring warnings and omens, Caesar goes to the Senate on the Ides of March. After the assassination, Mark Antony turns the people against the conspirators with a brilliant funeral speech, and war follows.

Shakespeare's Roman tragedy explores power, honour, friendship, persuasion and the unforeseen consequences of political violence. Although named after Caesar, the play centres largely on Brutus and his moral dilemma.

Julius Caesar was written in 1599 and was among the first plays performed at the new Globe Theatre; a Swiss traveller, Thomas Platter, saw it there in September 1599. Shakespeare drew mainly on Thomas North's translation of Plutarch's Lives. The play was first printed in the First Folio of 1623. This edition offers the English text (from the First Folio, in its original spelling), the French translation by François Guizot and the German translation by August Wilhelm von Schlegel.

books.title: As You Like It
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.desc: Banished from court, the witty Rosalind disguises herself as a young man in the Forest of Arden, where she meets Orlando, who is in love with her.
about: Duke Frederick has usurped his brother's dukedom, and the old Duke lives in exile in the Forest of Arden with his loyal followers. When Frederick banishes his niece Rosalind as well, she escapes to the forest disguised as a young man, Ganymede, with her cousin Celia and the jester Touchstone. There she meets Orlando, a young man fleeing his cruel brother, who has fallen in love with her and is hanging poems on the trees.

This pastoral comedy plays with disguise, love and the contrast between court and country life. Rosalind is one of Shakespeare's wittiest heroines, and the melancholy Jaques speaks the famous lines beginning "All the world's a stage".

As You Like It was written around 1599 and first printed in the First Folio of 1623. This edition offers the English text (from the First Folio, in its original spelling), the French translation by François Guizot and the German translation by August Wilhelm von Schlegel.

books.title: The Taming of the Shrew
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.desc: In Padua, the fortune-seeking Petruchio sets out to marry and 'tame' the sharp-tongued Katherina, so that her sweet younger sister may wed.
about: A drunken tinker, Christopher Sly, is tricked by a lord into believing he is a nobleman, and a play is performed for him. In Padua, the wealthy Baptista will not let his gentle younger daughter Bianca marry, despite her many suitors, until her elder sister Katherina, famous for her fierce temper, is married. Petruchio, a gentleman from Verona who has come "to wive it wealthily", decides to woo and tame her.

The play is full of farce, disguises and verbal sparring. Its central idea of a husband "taming" his wife reflects the attitudes of its time, and critics and audiences have long debated how seriously it is meant to be taken.
The Taming of the Shrew was written between 1590 and 1592 and first printed in the First Folio of 1623. This edition follows the First Folio text in its original spelling.
